resources.string: Pick your Budokai Tenkaichi 3 ISO (USA release, SLUS-21678). The app checks the image and unpacks the game data, like the PC port\'s setup. Nothing is downloaded: the data comes from your own disc.

This is not the unmodified USA release (a translation or a mod). Its files are used as they are, but the engine runs the original game program: what a mod changed in the game\'s code, rather than in its files, does not apply, and some mods may not work.

Every character, stage, song and item, and maximum Zeni. It is the debug function the developers left in the game, the same one as in the PC port.
Will be applied the next time the game starts

The unlock is written to the game\'s save (memory card) and cannot be undone by the app. It is applied once, when the game starts, and the switch turns itself off again.\n\nPCSX2 cheats (.pnach) do not apply here: Dragon Rage runs the game\'s code natively, not an emulator.
The game\'s save will change the next time the game starts. Copy the saves folder if you want to keep your current progress.
They apply the next time the game starts
1x is the PS2\'s own resolution. On phones and handhelds, 2x or 3x is usually the sweet spot; on weaker GPUs (Mali, Adreno 6xx), try 1.25x to 1.75x.
FXAA smooths jagged edges. FSR and Snapdragon GSR upscale with sharper edges: best with an internal resolution below the screen\'s (1x to 2x), so they also help weaker GPUs.
The black line around the fighters
Shows a fighter hidden behind scenery
The haze that colours distant things
The bloom around bright things and the sky\'s glare
The soft focus on distant scenery
Automatic: they hide as soon as a physical controller is used (the Odin\'s own, a Bluetooth pad) and come back when you touch the screen.

The game computes a fight 30 times a second, as on the PS2; with this, pictures are drawn in between (frame interpolation), for 60 or 120 a second. The fight itself and online play are unchanged. It costs about twice the GPU work: for strong GPUs. Experimental: pictures are left out at camera cuts.
Screen: the phone\'s own shape, so the fight fills it. Wide shapes show more of the scene to the sides (nothing is stretched); the menus are drawn for 4:3 and are widened.

How finished pictures reach the screen. Automatic: Mailbox where the device has it. FIFO (VSync) waits for the screen\'s refresh: no tearing, a little more latency, steadier pacing on some devices. Mailbox: no tearing, no wait. Immediate: lowest latency, may tear. Used the next time the game starts.
Uses your wallpaper\'s colours instead of Goku\'s

Android port of Tenkaichi3Decomp, the native PC port of Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 built on the BT3-Decompiled decompilation. Not affiliated with the game\'s developers, publishers or rights holders, and contains no game data: your own copy is needed.
The on-screen controller: when it shows, its look, its layout and macros
A short buzz when a button is pressed
The left stick starts where your thumb lands, anywhere on the lower left
Drag a control to move it. Tap it to select it: − and + resize it, α− and α+ adjust opacity, Hide hides it, Reset restores defaults. With nothing selected, size and opacity apply to all controls.
A macro is a button of your own on the screen that plays a sequence: a combo, or several buttons at once. Each step holds its buttons for a time; a step with no buttons is a pause.
Plays again for as long as the button is held (turbo)

For Snapdragon (Adreno) GPUs: another Vulkan driver, such as Turnip or a newer Qualcomm driver, from an AdrenoTools .zip. It can make the game start or run better where the phone\'s own driver fails. If the game does not start with it, choose System driver again.

It installs over this version and keeps your game data, settings and saves. Open the app again afterwards.
Android needs your permission for Dragon Rage to install the update. Tap the button, turn on \"Allow from this source\", then come back: the update continues by itself.
Could not check for updates. Check the connection.

In a clash of two beams or two rushes, tap or mash the Square (melee) button instead of turning the stick round. Works with the on-screen controls and with a physical controller. Also in the in-game window (Controls tab).

Game-specific: buttons for the game\'s own actions (target, Ki, melee, guard, dash…) in a thumb-friendly cluster, with a menu mode. Classic: the plain console pad (sticks, d-pad, four face buttons, shoulders). Each layout keeps its own placements.
Add a Play shortcut to the home screen
Creates an icon on the home screen that starts the game directly, without opening the app. The app icon\'s long-press menu has a Play entry too.
Shortcut requested: confirm it in the window that Android shows.
This launcher does not offer pinned shortcuts. Long-press the app icon: there is a Play entry.

Menu buttons in the menus and fight buttons in a fight, switched by itself. The MENU / FIGHT button on the screen still changes it by hand (for the pause menu in a fight, for example). Game-specific layout only.

Automatic: Vulkan, the faster one on nearly every GPU (0.5.0 chose OpenGL ES for Mali, which turned out much slower in fights there). OpenGL ES stays for GPUs whose Vulkan driver fails; it has no depth clamping and no screen filters (FXAA, FSR, GSR).
This zip uses a compression the app cannot read (LZMA, Zstandard or a password). Pack it again as a normal .zip (\"Deflate\", no password), for example with 7-Zip or ZArchiver.
Not enough space: this pack takes %1$s unpacked and the device has %2$s free.
The device ran out of space while unpacking (%1$s unpacked). Free some space and try again; nothing of this pack was kept.
Custom Vulkan drivers for Snapdragon and Mali GPUs

Your GPU is %1$s. MaliSX2, the ARMSX2 emulator\'s own Vulkan driver for Mali, is built for it: install it below and the game uses it with Vulkan. It was made for a PlayStation 2 emulator, so some parts of the game may not work with it yet: if the game does not start or shows a black screen, choose System driver again. Send the log either way, it helps.
Your GPU is %1$s. Custom drivers only work on Adreno (Snapdragon) GPUs and on the Mali GPUs MaliSX2 is built for (G52, G57, G68, G77, G78, G615, G715); on this device the system\'s driver is used.
The latest releases of the people who build them, straight from GitHub. A driver is installed and chosen in one tap; if the game does not start with it, choose the system\'s driver above.
Could not reach GitHub. Check the connection and try again (GitHub allows 60 lookups an hour without a login).
No driver packages in the latest releases.
Recommended settings for your GPU\'s tier, made to keep fights at a steady 30 pictures a second. Shown before anything changes.
Every few seconds the game notes its speed in its log (no cost you can feel). On by default; it is what a report about slowness needs.
No numbers yet: play a fight, then come back here.
Last run, fights: %1$d%% speed on average, %2$d%% at worst, %3$.1f pictures/s
Full speed: the game ran as on the console.
Below full speed at times. Try the recommended settings above, a lower resolution, or Precise depth off.

Optimizations applied. They count from the next start of the game.
%1$s is not in the list yet: the settings stay as they are. Send your log on Discord so it can be added.
Skip pictures instead of slowing down
Exact overlap of surfaces in one plane (waterfalls, marks on the ground). Off is faster on weaker GPUs, with a rare flicker.
Skip pictures instead of slowing down
When the GPU is behind, the game keeps its speed and leaves a picture out.
For Mali-G52 class GPUs: the renderer on its own thread and the glow and the sky\'s glare off (turning it on sets both to 0). Takes effect the next time the game starts.
Lite mode: render thread, glow and glare off
This device has too little CPU for BT4: the fight will run below normal speed.
How the game opens. Portrait puts the picture at the top and the controls under it; Automatic follows the way the device is held.
Play against Android and Nintendo Switch players on Dragon Net (with Ranked), or against PC players. See how it works and what to do when it does not connect.

1. In the game's main menu choose Dragon Net Battle. Tap your name (top right, or Start) to change it.
2. Create room: choose the battle (single, team, DP 10/15/20) and open it; a 6-character code appears. Tap it to copy and send it to your friend.
3. Join room: type or paste the code and join. The host's battle rules are used.
4. Quick match: choose the battle and search; the first player waiting in the same queue is your rival. A search ends by itself after three minutes.
5. When the two games connect, the match starts by itself: both get the same roster with everything unlocked, and your own save is left alone. Leaving the match brings you back to the menu.
6. Only button presses travel: both games compute the fight, with rollback for late presses. Wi-Fi near the router gives the steadiest fights.
7. Both players need the same game (the USA disc, SLUS-21678) and a compatible version: Dragon Net between Dragon Rage 0.8+ and DBT-NX with the PC port's 0.1.37; PC mode with the PC port's newest release.

• "The Dragon Net service does not take this version yet": the service is updated shortly after a release; meanwhile choose Play against: PC.
• "Update Dragon Rage" / "asks for release 0.1.xx" (PC mode): the PC port released a new version; play on Dragon Net until the next Dragon Rage.
• "The other game is a different version": you and your rival are on different versions; both update.
• "Nobody searched in the last three minutes": nobody was in that queue; try another battle type, or create a room and share the code.
• "The two games could not reach each other": switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, turn off VPN, data saver and private DNS, and try again. Some mobile networks block direct connections; then the relay is used and it may be slower.
• Room not found: check the 6 characters (0 and O, 1 and I) and that both chose the same Play against.
• "Too many requests" / "busy": the free services have hourly limits. Wait a few minutes.
• Lag or stutters: both on Wi-Fi near the router; the speed meter (Settings) shows the connection during a match.
Could not reach the online service
No internet, or the matchmaking service did not answer. Offline play is not affected; try again later with the refresh button.
Server busy (daily limit), try again later. Offline play is not affected.

The online service now asks for the PC port\'s release %1$s or newer, and this Dragon Rage is %2$s. Online matches will not start until you install the latest Dragon Rage (GitHub releases). Everything offline keeps working.

The matchmaking service is now only accepting the PC port\'s signed builds, and Dragon Rage is not one of them. Quick match and room codes will not work for now; a direct connection (Join → address and port) between two Dragon Rage phones still works.
This Dragon Rage (release %1$s) is accepted by the matchmaking service: quick match, rooms with a code and direct connections all work, also against PC players on the same release.
Online is played from the game\'s menu: open Dragon Net Battle and pick Create room, Join room, Quick match or Ranked. A Wi-Fi connection gives the steadiest fights.
The game closed: a problem with the game data

The game stopped because a file of the imported disc image is missing, damaged or modified. Dragon Rage needs an unmodified USA disc image (SLUS-21678). Import the ISO again (Game data → Import); if it was modified or a mod changed its files, use a clean dump.
The game closed: not enough memory
The phone could not give the game the memory it needs. Close other apps, restart the phone and try again; a lower resolution and turning off texture packs also help.
The game closed: the engine did not start
The game\'s engine could not start on this phone. Try the other renderer (Settings → Renderer), and if you use a custom driver, go back to the system driver.
The last run ended with a crash. If it happens again, export the log and send it to us (Discord or GitHub) with your phone\'s model. Switching the renderer or the GPU driver often helps.
This disc image is modified in a way Dragon Rage cannot run (its DBZP.BIN is smaller than the game needs). Use an unmodified USA dump (SLUS-21678).
%1$s was not copied completely (storage full or the file could not be read). Free some space and import again.

Experimental, off by default. Keeps a compressed copy of texture-pack images in the format phone GPUs read (Mali, Adreno…), made on the CPU in the background the first time each is used: less memory, but the conversion takes CPU time while you play.

On Mali GPUs OpenGL ES is several times slower in fights than Vulkan (a Mali-G52: about 4 pictures a second against 12 to 26, with the game at full speed). Use Automatic unless Vulkan does not start on this phone.

1. Download an HD pack made for this game in PCSX2 or AetherSX2/NetherSX2 (the USA release, SLUS-21678). Packs for the Japanese or European release do not match.
2. Tap Add pack and pick the pack's .zip (do not rename the files inside). A pack that came as .rar or .7z: extract it and pack the folder again as .zip first (ZArchiver or RAR on the phone, 7-Zip on a PC). Unpacked, a pack can take several times the zip's size: the large SLUS-21678 one needs about 11 GB free.
3. The pack appears below with how many textures it has. Leave "Use texture packs" on and start a fight: the textures change as the game loads them.
If the pack does not install, or installs but nothing changes in a fight, the app saves a log in Downloads by itself and tells you its name: send that file to us.
Something else wrong with textures? Save a log here and send it to us on Discord or GitHub.
This texture pack could not be installed
The log was saved in Downloads as %1$s. Send this file to the developer (Discord or GitHub) so we can fix it.
The log could not be saved by itself: use Debug → Export log.
The texture pack was not used

The game played a fight without using any texture from your pack. Usually the pack is for another release of the game (Japanese or European) or is not a PCSX2 pack. Check that it is for the USA release (SLUS-21678); if it is, send us the log.

Dragon Net: Dragon Rage and the Nintendo Switch port (DBT-NX) on a service of their own, with Ranked (Elo) and the players online; it does not depend on the PC port\'s releases. PC: rooms and quick match on the PC port\'s service, which only lets in its newest release. You can also switch it in the game\'s Dragon Net Battle screen (Y on a controller).
Used in casual matches and rooms. Ranked always uses automatic delay.
Used in casual matches and rooms. Ranked always uses rollback up to 8 frames.
Android and Switch play together: rooms with a code, quick match and Ranked, from Dragon Net Battle in the game\'s main menu.
The Dragon Net service does not take this version\'s netcode yet: it is updated by its keeper shortly after a release. Meanwhile you can play against PC (Settings → Online) or by direct connection.

• Android + Switch (Dragon Net, the default): Dragon Rage and the Nintendo Switch port (DBT-NX) on a service of their own. It has Ranked (Elo) and the count of players online, and it does not stop when the PC port releases a new version.
• PC: rooms and quick match against the PC port, on the PC port's service. That service only lets in its newest release, so after a new PC release this mode waits for the next Dragon Rage.
• Choose it in the game (Dragon Net Battle → Play against, or Y on a controller) or here in Settings → Online. Both players must choose the same one: a Dragon Net room code does not exist on the PC service, and the other way round.
• The card above says whether the chosen one is working now.

• Your profile is made the first time you open Ranked: rank (Bronze to Master), Elo points, wins, losses and position. It belongs to this phone; uninstalling the app or clearing its data starts a new one.
• Search for a rival (single or team): you are paired with a player of your level; the search widens while you wait. Fights have no time limit and run at the standard speed.
• At the end both games send the result. Points change only when both agree; if they differ, nobody gets points. Leaving a ranked fight before its end (or closing the game) counts as a loss.
• Ranking shows the best players; Update profile reloads yours.
• General chat: switched off for now (it comes back in a later version).\n• Players online: an approximate count of who has the online screen open now, on Android and Switch.

Right after the problem, come back to the app and press Send log: it saves a report in Downloads (the device, the game\'s last three runs and everything the app did) and opens the share sheet. Send it on our Discord with a line about what you tried and against whom.
The original game (USA disc). Online with Dragon Net, mods, stages, songs, cheats and custom drivers.
Team BT4\'s mod: new characters, forms and stages. Experimental: its own engine (the mod recompiled), drawn by ARMSX2\'s renderer (Dragon Rage\'s is an experimental option).
Each game keeps its own disc image, saves, textures and settings. You can switch from the menu (Game) at any time.

Pick your image of Team BT4\'s mod: SLUS-219.78, Beta 14 Rev2 (another version does not work: the game was recompiled for that one). Only its boot files are copied; the rest is read from the image where it is, so keep it in its folder.
The Budokai Tenkaichi 4 engine is in this build.
This build does not have the Budokai Tenkaichi 4 engine yet (libbt4.so). The image can be set up already.
Tells Android how long each frame takes (Android 13 and newer), so the CPU stays fast in heavy moments instead of slowing down between frames. From the next start.

Asks Android for steady clocks the phone can hold for a long time, instead of the highest ones (where the phone supports it). Less heat and fewer drops in long sessions; the top speed can be a little lower.
The mod draws its picture in 16:9: 16:9 shows it as Team BT4 made it. 4:3 is the PlayStation 2 frame as it is (people look thinner); Screen stretches it to the whole screen.

The fight runs at 60 pictures a second (BT3-Recomp\'s mode, as in the mod\'s PC build). Heavy for the CPU: where the device cannot hold 60 (below 57 a second for 3 s of a fight), it goes back to 30 by itself.
This device could not hold 60 fps in BT4\'s fights; back to 30.

ARMSX2 (default): the PlayStation 2 emulator\'s renderer (PCSX2\'s, with ARMSX2\'s fixes for Mali and Adreno), the most faithful picture. Dragon Rage (experimental): Budokai Tenkaichi 3\'s renderer, with faults in some of BT4\'s scenery. Both use the resolution, the shape and the Vulkan or OpenGL ES choice above. From the next start.
This image is not Budokai Tenkaichi 4 (it has no SLUS_219.78). It needs Team BT4\'s mod, Beta 14 Rev2.

This image is another version of the mod: the game was recompiled for Beta 14 Rev2 (SLUS-219.78). The SLUS_219.78 of your image has %1$d bytes (SHA-256 %2$s…); this one needs 2115688 bytes (224525C5…). A file named Rev2 can still hold another build: get the Beta 14 Rev2 image from the Team BT4 release.
Android did not let the app keep reading this image. Move it to Downloads or the phone\'s storage and pick it again.

This file is a compressed %1$s, not the disc image itself. Extract it first (ZArchiver, for example) and pick the .iso inside. CHD and CSO images must be turned back into .iso (chdman / maxcso on a PC).
This file is a web page, not the game: the download link saved its page instead of the file. Download the ISO again and pick the .iso.
This file is too small to be the game (%1$s; the ISO is about 3 GB). It may be an unfinished download or a shortcut.
